metadata.title: zERC20 Privacy Token Protocol - Audit Map Batch 2
metadata.methodology: 5-phase attack vector analysis with counterexample construction

audit_results.title: Verifier authorization on teleport minting

input_validation_bypass.attack_vector: Attempt to call zERC20.teleport() from an address other than the authorized verifier
input_validation_bypass.analysis: The teleport() function checks `if (msg.sender != verifier()) revert OnlyVerifier()` at line 144. This explicit check ensures only the registered verifier address can mint via teleport. No bypass path exists since verifier() reads from storage and the check is the first operation.

state_transition_violation.attack_vector: Attempt to call teleport() when verifier address is not set or is zero
state_transition_violation.analysis: setVerifier() at line 168 requires `if (newVerifier == address(0)) revert ZeroAddress()`. However, the initial state after deployment has verifier as address(0) until setVerifier is called. During this window, teleport() would always revert since msg.sender != address(0) would only pass if someone managed to call from address(0) which is impossible.

resource_exhaustion.attack_vector: DoS via repeated teleport calls consuming gas
resource_exhaustion.analysis: Teleport calls _mint which has O(1) complexity. Each teleport is independent. No unbounded loops exist. The function cannot be used for DoS by unauthorized callers since only verifier can call it.

faulty_error_handling.attack_vector: Attempt teleport with invalid parameters that might fail silently
faulty_error_handling.analysis: teleport() will revert with OnlyVerifier() for unauthorized callers. The _mint internal call and totalTeleported update happen atomically. No silent failures possible - either the entire operation succeeds or reverts.

race_conditions.attack_vector: Front-run verifier teleport call with setVerifier to redirect minting authority
race_conditions.analysis: setVerifier() is onlyOwner. If owner calls setVerifier while a teleport is pending, the teleport would revert with OnlyVerifier() since msg.sender (old verifier) != new verifier. This is safe behavior - no funds at risk. Owner operations are out of scope per trust model.

counterexample.scenario: Malicious actor deploys contract at predetermined address and attempts to call teleport()
counterexample.expected_result: Attack fails - only registered verifier can mint via teleport
counterexample.actual_behavior: Correctly prevented by verifier() check at line 144

guards_identified: OnlyVerifier modifier equivalent (if check) at zERC20.sol:144
ZeroAddress check in setVerifier at zERC20.sol:169
audit_results.rationale: Authorization check is present and correctly implemented. The verifier address must be set via owner-only setVerifier which prevents zero address. No bypass paths identified through static analysis.

audit_results.title: Teleport delta calculation correctness

input_validation_bypass.attack_vector: Submit proof with totalValue that bypasses delta calculation
input_validation_bypass.analysis: The delta is calculated as `uint256 diff = value - currentTotal` at line 378 after verifying `value > currentTotal` at line 377. The value comes from the ZK proof public inputs which are verified. No way to bypass - value is cryptographically bound to proof.

state_transition_violation.attack_vector: Teleport with value <= currentTotal to mint zero or negative tokens
state_transition_violation.analysis: Line 377 requires `value > currentTotal` (strict inequality). If value <= currentTotal, reverts with NothingToWithdraw. The subtraction at line 378 cannot underflow because value > currentTotal is enforced. Solidity 0.8+ checked arithmetic provides additional safety.

resource_exhaustion.attack_vector: Submit proofs with very small deltas repeatedly
resource_exhaustion.analysis: Each teleport requires a valid ZK proof which is computationally expensive to generate. The monotonicity check prevents replay. Small deltas still require full proof verification cost. No economic incentive for DoS since attacker pays gas.

faulty_error_handling.attack_vector: Cause teleport to succeed but mint wrong amount
faulty_error_handling.analysis: After computing diff, line 379 updates `$.totalTeleported[recipient] += diff` and line 381 calls `IzERC20($.token).teleport(recipientAddr, diff)`. The same diff value is used for both operations atomically. If zERC20.teleport() reverts, the storage update is also reverted.

race_conditions.attack_vector: Two concurrent teleports for same recipient causing incorrect delta
race_conditions.analysis: totalTeleported[recipient] is read at line 376 and written at line 379. In a single transaction context, this is atomic. If two transactions race, both read the same currentTotal, but the second would fail monotonicity check since first would have updated totalTeleported. No double-spend possible.

counterexample.scenario: Attempt to mint more tokens than the proof authorizes by manipulating delta calculation
preconditions: Valid proof exists for recipient with totalValue=100
attack_steps: Attempt to modify delta in transit - impossible due to atomic execution
counterexample.expected_result: Exactly 50 tokens minted, totalTeleported updated to 100
counterexample.actual_behavior: Correctly mints delta amount only, updates monotonic counter

guards_identified: Strict monotonicity check (value > currentTotal) at Verifier.sol:377
Delta computation after monotonicity check at Verifier.sol:378
Atomic storage update and external call at Verifier.sol:379-381
audit_results.rationale: Delta calculation is mathematically correct with proper ordering: monotonicity check before subtraction prevents underflow. Atomic execution prevents race conditions. ZK proof binds value to proof validity.

audit_results.title: Owner authorization on UUPS upgrade (OUT OF SCOPE)

input_validation_bypass.attack_vector: Attempt UUPS upgrade from non-owner address
input_validation_bypass.analysis: _authorizeUpgrade has `onlyOwner` modifier. Non-owner calls revert. This is OUT OF SCOPE per trust model - owner compromise is not considered a vulnerability.

state_transition_violation.attack_vector: Upgrade to malicious implementation
state_transition_violation.analysis: Owner can upgrade to any implementation. No validation of new implementation address. This is by design - owner is trusted. OUT OF SCOPE per trust model.

resource_exhaustion.analysis: Upgrade operations are not susceptible to DoS patterns.

faulty_error_handling.analysis: UUPS pattern from OpenZeppelin validates new implementation is a contract in the base implementation. Owner responsibility.

counterexample.scenario: Non-owner attempts to upgrade contract implementation
counterexample.actual_behavior: Correctly reverts for non-owner callers

guards_identified: UUPS implementation validation in OpenZeppelin base
audit_results.rationale: OUT OF SCOPE per trust model. Owner operations are trusted. onlyOwner modifier correctly restricts upgrade authority.

audit_results.title: Owner authorization on minter change (OUT OF SCOPE)

input_validation_bypass.attack_vector: Attempt to set minter from non-owner address
input_validation_bypass.analysis: setMinter has `onlyOwner` modifier at line 177. Non-owner calls revert. OUT OF SCOPE per trust model.

state_transition_violation.attack_vector: Set minter to zero address to disable minting
state_transition_violation.analysis: Unlike setVerifier, setMinter ALLOWS setting to address(0) per spec comment at line 175: 'the spec allows disabling the minter by setting address(0) on chains without deposits'. This is intentional design.

resource_exhaustion.analysis: Owner operation, not susceptible to DoS.

faulty_error_handling.analysis: Simple storage write, no error conditions beyond authorization.

counterexample.scenario: Non-owner attempts to grant themselves minting authority
counterexample.actual_behavior: Correctly reverts for non-owner callers

guards_identified: onlyOwner modifier on setMinter at zERC20.sol:177
audit_results.rationale: OUT OF SCOPE per trust model. Note: minter CAN be set to zero address by design to disable minting on certain chains.

audit_results.title: Owner authorization on token registration (OUT OF SCOPE)

input_validation_bypass.attack_vector: Attempt to register token from non-owner address
input_validation_bypass.analysis: registerToken has `onlyOwner` modifier at line 154. Non-owner calls revert. OUT OF SCOPE per trust model.

state_transition_violation.attack_vector: Register token with zero verifier or token address
state_transition_violation.analysis: Validates: `if (info.verifier == address(0)) revert ZeroVerifier()` at 155, `if (info.token == address(0)) revert ZeroToken()` at 156, `if (info.chainId == 0) revert InvalidChainId()` at 157. Proper validation present.

resource_exhaustion.attack_vector: Register maximum tokens to fill capacity
resource_exhaustion.analysis: MAX_LEAVES check at line 160: `if ($.transferRoots.length >= MAX_LEAVES) revert HubCapacityReached()`. Maximum 64 tokens (height-6 tree). Owner-only so not exploitable by attackers.

faulty_error_handling.analysis: Duplicate check at line 159: `if ($.eidToPosition[info.eid] != 0) revert TokenAlreadyRegistered(info.eid)`. Prevents duplicate registration.

counterexample.scenario: Attacker tries to register malicious token
counterexample.actual_behavior: Correctly reverts for non-owner

audit_results.rationale: OUT OF SCOPE per trust model. Function has comprehensive input validation despite being owner-only. No vulnerabilities identified.

audit_results.title: Owner authorization on verifier rotation (OUT OF SCOPE)

input_validation_bypass.attack_vector: Attempt to set verifiers from non-owner address
input_validation_bypass.analysis: setVerifiers has `onlyOwner` modifier at line 481. Non-owner calls revert. OUT OF SCOPE per trust model.

state_transition_violation.attack_vector: Set any verifier to zero address
state_transition_violation.analysis: Comprehensive zero address check at lines 482-488 for all five verifier addresses. Reverts with ZeroAddress() if any is zero. Proper validation.

resource_exhaustion.analysis: Owner operation, not susceptible to DoS.

faulty_error_handling.analysis: Simple storage writes with event emission.

counterexample.scenario: Non-owner attempts to rotate verifiers to accept forged proofs
attack_steps: Call setVerifiers with malicious verifier addresses
counterexample.actual_behavior: Correctly reverts for non-owner

guards_identified: Zero address validation for all 5 verifiers at Verifier.sol:482-488
audit_results.rationale: OUT OF SCOPE per trust model. All five verifier addresses validated against zero. Atomic update with event emission.

audit_results.title: Owner authorization on fee configuration (OUT OF SCOPE)

input_validation_bypass.attack_vector: Attempt to set fee params from non-fee-manager address
input_validation_bypass.analysis: setFeeParams has `onlyRole(FEE_MANAGER_ROLE)` modifier at line 184. Non-role-holder calls revert. OUT OF SCOPE per trust model (FEE_MANAGER_ROLE granted to owner).

state_transition_violation.attack_vector: Set invalid fee parameters causing arithmetic issues
state_transition_violation.analysis: validateFeeParams() called at line 185 before storage update. This validates parameter bounds. See IncentiveLib for validation logic.

faulty_error_handling.analysis: validateFeeParams reverts on invalid params.

counterexample.scenario: Non-admin sets extreme fee parameters
counterexample.actual_behavior: Correctly reverts for non-role-holder

audit_results.rationale: OUT OF SCOPE per trust model. Fee parameter validation present via validateFeeParams().

audit_results.title: Proof soundness guarantees validity at on-chain verification

input_validation_bypass.attack_vector: Submit proof generated by malicious prover
input_validation_bypass.analysis: All proof submissions go through on-chain verification: IRootDecider.verifyOpaqueNovaProof at line 274/325, IWithdrawVerifier.verifyProof at line 347. Invalid proofs revert with InvalidProof(). Prover is NOT trusted - cryptographic verification ensures soundness.

state_transition_violation.attack_vector: Submit valid-looking proof with invalid public inputs
state_transition_violation.analysis: Public inputs are extracted from proof bytes and verified as part of ZK verification. The verifier contracts check proof against public inputs. Invalid inputs cause proof verification failure.

resource_exhaustion.attack_vector: Submit many invalid proofs to waste gas
resource_exhaustion.analysis: Proof verification is expensive. Invalid proofs cost attacker gas with no benefit. No state change occurs on invalid proof. Standard blockchain economics apply.

faulty_error_handling.attack_vector: Cause verifier contract to return false instead of reverting
faulty_error_handling.analysis: All three verification calls use require() which reverts on false return. No path allows processing to continue after failed verification.

race_conditions.analysis: Proof verification is stateless operation per call.

counterexample.scenario: Malicious prover generates forged proof to mint tokens
counterexample.actual_behavior: Correctly rejected by cryptographic verification

guards_identified: require() wrapper on all verification calls
audit_results.rationale: Prover is UNTRUSTED by design. Security guaranteed by ZKP soundness, not prover trust. All proofs verified on-chain before any state changes.

audit_results.title: Groth16 proof structure matches on-chain verifier expectations

input_validation_bypass.attack_vector: Submit malformed proof bytes that decode incorrectly
input_validation_bypass.analysis: Proof decoding uses abi.decode with expected types. For singleTeleport at line 343-344: (uint256[2], uint256[2][2], uint256[2], uint256[3]). Malformed bytes cause abi.decode to revert.

state_transition_violation.attack_vector: Submit proof with different structure than expected
state_transition_violation.analysis: Fixed-size array decoding enforces exact structure. Nova proofs decoded as uint256[32] or uint256[34]. Groth16 proofs decoded as specific tuple. Any structure mismatch causes revert.

faulty_error_handling.analysis: abi.decode reverts if calldata is insufficient for expected types. No silent failure.

counterexample.scenario: Submit proof with wrong curve point encoding
preconditions: Have proof bytes with invalid G1/G2 point encoding
attack_steps: abi.decode succeeds but verifier rejects invalid curve points
counterexample.actual_behavior: Groth16 verifier validates curve points as part of verification

guards_identified: abi.decode with fixed types at Verifier.sol:313, 343-344
audit_results.rationale: Proof structure enforced by abi.decode. Curve point validity checked by Groth16 verifier. No format mismatch vulnerability.

audit_results.title: Merkle proof validity guaranteed by ZK circuit verification

input_validation_bypass.attack_vector: Submit invalid Merkle proof from malicious indexer
input_validation_bypass.analysis: Merkle proofs are verified inside the ZK circuit, not on-chain. Invalid Merkle path causes circuit to produce unsatisfiable constraints. No valid ZK proof can be generated for invalid Merkle path. On-chain only verifies the resulting ZK proof.

state_transition_violation.attack_vector: Merkle proof that passes circuit but doesn't match on-chain root
state_transition_violation.analysis: The transfer root is a public input to the ZK proof and is verified against provedTransferRoots or globalTransferRoots at line 366-368. Root must match or teleport reverts.

faulty_error_handling.analysis: Invalid Merkle proofs cause proof generation failure, not on-chain error.

counterexample.scenario: Malicious indexer provides false Merkle path to user
attack_steps: User generates ZK proof with wrong Merkle path
counterexample.expected_result: Cannot generate valid proof with invalid Merkle path
counterexample.actual_behavior: ZK circuit enforces Merkle path validity

guards_identified: Transfer root public input binding at Verifier.sol:366-368
audit_results.rationale: Indexer is SEMI_TRUSTED - invalid Merkle proofs cause proof generation failure, not security breach. ZK circuit enforces correctness.

audit_results.title: Merkle structure matches on-chain hash chain computation

input_validation_bypass.attack_vector: Indexer uses different hash function than on-chain
input_validation_bypass.analysis: Hash chain uses ShaHashChainLib.compute() at zERC20.sol:157 which implements SHA-256 with 248-bit truncation. Indexer must match this exactly or proofs will fail. This is a configuration/implementation detail to verify.

state_transition_violation.attack_vector: Different leaf encoding between indexer and contract
state_transition_violation.analysis: ShaHashChainLib.compute takes (hashChain, from, to, value). Indexer must encode leaves identically. Mismatch causes proof failure, not security breach.

faulty_error_handling.analysis: Mismatch causes proof failure.

counterexample.scenario: Indexer uses keccak256 instead of SHA-256
preconditions: Indexer misconfigured to use wrong hash
attack_steps: User requests Merkle proof from indexer
ZK proof generated with wrong leaf values
counterexample.actual_behavior: Hash mismatch causes proof failure, not incorrect minting

guards_identified: ZK circuit must use matching hash function
audit_results.rationale: Hash function consistency between indexer, on-chain, and ZK circuit is critical but cannot be verified statically. Requires integration testing.

audit_results.title: No unauthorized third minting pathway exists

input_validation_bypass.attack_vector: Find hidden minting function in zERC20
input_validation_bypass.analysis: zERC20 has exactly two external functions that mint: mint() at line 185 (onlyMinter) and teleport() at line 143 (onlyVerifier). Both have access control. _mint is internal. _credit (LayerZero OFT) at line 123 also mints but is internal callback for cross-chain transfers.

state_transition_violation.attack_vector: Exploit inheritance to access _mint directly
state_transition_violation.analysis: zERC20 inherits from OFTCoreUpgradeable, ERC20PermitUpgradeable, UUPSUpgradeable, IzERC20. _mint is inherited from ERC20Upgradeable but is internal. No public/external wrapper except mint() and teleport(). _credit() is internal and called by OFT receive flow.

faulty_error_handling.analysis: Not applicable.

counterexample.scenario: Find third minting pathway in zERC20
attack_steps: Found: mint() line 187, teleport() line 146, _credit() line 135
counterexample.actual_behavior: mint() requires onlyMinter, teleport() requires onlyVerifier, _credit() is internal OFT callback

guards_identified: _credit is internal, called by OFT _lzReceive flow
audit_results.rationale: CRITICAL CHECK. Three paths to _mint found: mint (minter-only), teleport (verifier-only), _credit (internal OFT). Need to verify _credit cannot be exploited via LayerZero OFT receive path.

audit_results.title: Complete cross-chain message isolation via EID validation

input_validation_bypass.attack_vector: Send cross-chain message from unregistered EID
input_validation_bypass.analysis: Hub._lzReceive checks `if (pos == 0) revert TokenNotRegistered(origin.srcEid)` at line 318. Verifier._lzReceive checks `require(origin.srcEid == $.hubEid, InvalidHubSource(origin.srcEid))` at line 440. Both validate source EID before processing.

state_transition_violation.attack_vector: Spoof srcEid in Origin struct
state_transition_violation.analysis: Origin struct is populated by LayerZero endpoint, not by caller. Spoofing requires compromising LayerZero protocol itself. LayerZero is SEMI_TRUSTED per trust model but EID is verified regardless.

resource_exhaustion.attack_vector: Send many messages from unauthorized EIDs
resource_exhaustion.analysis: Messages from unauthorized EIDs revert immediately. Attacker pays cross-chain fees with no state change. Not economically viable DoS.

faulty_error_handling.attack_vector: Message from unknown EID silently ignored
faulty_error_handling.analysis: Both use revert (Hub: TokenNotRegistered, Verifier: InvalidHubSource) not return. No silent failures.

race_conditions.attack_vector: Race between peer registration and message receipt
race_conditions.analysis: If peer unregistered between message send and receive, message reverts with TokenNotRegistered. Safe behavior.

counterexample.scenario: Attacker sends malicious root from unauthorized chain
preconditions: Attacker controls verifier on chain with EID 999
attack_steps: Send LayerZero message to Hub from EID 999
counterexample.actual_behavior: Correctly reverts for unregistered source EID

guards_identified: eidToPosition check in Hub._lzReceive at Hub.sol:317-318
hubEid check in Verifier._lzReceive at Verifier.sol:440
audit_results.rationale: CRITICAL CHECK. Both Hub and Verifier validate source EID. Hub checks against registered tokens, Verifier checks against configured hubEid. Complete isolation achieved.

audit_results.title: STATE-USER-IDLE transitions require validation by receiving components

input_validation_bypass.attack_vector: Call user-facing functions with malicious inputs
input_validation_bypass.analysis: User entry points: wrap() validates amount>0, receiver!=0, msg.value; unwrap() validates amount>0, receiver!=0; transfer() inherited from OZ ERC20 validates balances. All user inputs validated before state changes.

state_transition_violation.attack_vector: User directly modifies contract state
state_transition_violation.analysis: No public setters for critical state. All state modifications go through validated function paths.

resource_exhaustion.analysis: Standard blockchain economics - user pays gas. ReentrancyGuard on LiquidityManager functions.

faulty_error_handling.attack_vector: Input validation silently accepts bad values
faulty_error_handling.analysis: wrap: ZeroAmount, ZeroReceiver errors. unwrap: ZeroAmount, ZeroReceiver errors. All use revert, no silent failures.

counterexample.scenario: User attempts to wrap without providing underlying tokens
attack_steps: Call wrap(100, receiver) with 0 token balance
counterexample.actual_behavior: Correctly reverts due to insufficient balance

audit_results.rationale: All user entry points have appropriate input validation. UNTRUSTED->IN_SCOPE boundary properly protected.

audit_results.title: STATE-USER-HAS-UNDERLYING only reachable via valid unwrap completion

input_validation_bypass.attack_vector: Obtain underlying tokens without burning zERC20
input_validation_bypass.analysis: _unwrap burns zERC20 at line 288 BEFORE transferring underlying at lines 290-297. No path transfers underlying without prior burn. Burn is called on msg.sender's balance.

state_transition_violation.attack_vector: Reentrancy to withdraw underlying multiple times
state_transition_violation.analysis: unwrap() has nonReentrant modifier. _unwrap is private. Even with callback from malicious token, reentrancy blocked. Additionally, zERC20 burn happens before underlying transfer (CEI pattern partial).

faulty_error_handling.analysis: Native transfer uses call{value} with success check at line 291-293. ERC20 uses safeTransfer which reverts on failure. No silent failures.

counterexample.scenario: User attempts to withdraw underlying without burning zERC20
attack_steps: ZERC20_TOKEN.burn fails due to insufficient balance
counterexample.actual_behavior: Correctly reverts when user lacks zERC20

guards_identified: zERC20 burn before underlying transfer at LiquidityManager.sol:288
Native transfer success check at LiquidityManager.sol:291-293
audit_results.rationale: Unwrap flow correctly enforces burn-before-transfer. Reentrancy protected. Only valid unwrap path leads to underlying possession.

audit_results.title: STATE-USER-HAS-ZERC20 only reachable via wrap or teleport completion

input_validation_bypass.attack_vector: Mint zERC20 without going through wrap or teleport
input_validation_bypass.analysis: mint() requires onlyMinter (LiquidityManager). teleport() requires onlyVerifier. _credit() is internal OFT callback. No other external/public minting paths exist.

state_transition_violation.attack_vector: Transfer creates tokens (violation of conservation)
state_transition_violation.analysis: ERC20 _transfer decrements sender and increments recipient by same amount. No token creation in transfer. Solidity 0.8+ prevents overflow/underflow.

faulty_error_handling.attack_vector: Mint without proper authorization silently succeeds
faulty_error_handling.analysis: Both use revert on authorization failure (OnlyMinter, OnlyVerifier). No silent bypass.

counterexample.scenario: Attacker finds third path to increase zERC20 balance
preconditions: Search all paths to balance increase
attack_steps: _credit requires valid OFT receive flow with peer validation
counterexample.actual_behavior: zERC20 balance only increases via wrap, teleport, or cross-chain OFT receive

guards_identified: _credit is internal OFT callback with peer validation
audit_results.rationale: CRITICAL. Only wrap (via minter mint) and teleport (via verifier) and OFT receive (_credit) can increase user zERC20 balance. All paths properly authorized.

audit_results.title: STATE-LM-AWAITING-WRAP enforces BN254 field constraints

input_validation_bypass.attack_vector: Wrap amount that exceeds 2^248-1
input_validation_bypass.analysis: _update hook checks `if (value > type(uint248).max) revert ValueTooLarge()` at line 154. This applies to ALL transfers including mints from wrap. No bypass possible.

state_transition_violation.attack_vector: Resulting balance exceeds MAX_VALUE after wrap
state_transition_violation.analysis: The check is on `value` (transfer amount), not resulting balance. However, if value <= MAX_VALUE and balance is already at MAX_VALUE, the resulting balance could exceed MAX_VALUE. POTENTIAL ISSUE: Balance check should be on resulting balance, not just value.

faulty_error_handling.analysis: Uses revert with custom error.

counterexample.scenario: Wrap amount that results in balance > 2^248-1
preconditions: Wrap amount such that balance + amount > MAX_VALUE
attack_steps: Check is on value (2 <= MAX_VALUE) so passes
counterexample.actual_behavior: NEEDS VERIFICATION - current check is on value not resulting balance

audit_results.rationale: The MAX_VALUE check is on transfer value, not resulting balance. Need to verify if ERC20 balance overflow protection or additional checks prevent resulting balance from exceeding MAX_VALUE. Solidity 0.8+ prevents uint256 overflow but 2^248-1 is smaller than uint256.max.

audit_results.title: ACTION-LM-CALCULATE-REWARD uses floor rounding for rewards

input_validation_bypass.attack_vector: Input amounts that cause incorrect reward calculation
input_validation_bypass.analysis: quoteWrapReward uses standard division which floors in Solidity. Need to verify IncentiveLib implementation uses floor for rewards (favorable to protocol).

state_transition_violation.attack_vector: Reward exceeds available feeSurplus
state_transition_violation.analysis: Reward is calculated then subtracted from feeSurplus at line 273: `if (reward > 0) $.feeSurplus -= reward`. If reward > feeSurplus, this underflows and reverts in Solidity 0.8+. The quoteWrapReward should cap reward at feeSurplus.

faulty_error_handling.attack_vector: Division by zero in reward calculation
faulty_error_handling.analysis: Need to verify IncentiveLib handles division by zero cases.

race_conditions.analysis: Reward calculated fresh in each transaction.

counterexample.scenario: Wrap with amount that produces fractional reward
counterexample.actual_behavior: Need to verify IncentiveLib rounding direction

audit_results.rationale: Rounding direction needs verification in IncentiveLib. Default Solidity division floors which is correct for rewards.

audit_results.title: ACTION-LM-PULL-LIQUIDITY transfers exact requested amount

input_validation_bypass.attack_vector: Fee-on-transfer token causes amount mismatch
input_validation_bypass.analysis: For ERC20: line 263 does safeTransferFrom, line 264 calculates received = balance_after - balance_before. This DOES handle FoT tokens. However, the reward is calculated on `received` not `amount`, so if FoT token is used, reward is based on actual received.

state_transition_violation.attack_vector: Transfer succeeds but contract receives less than expected
state_transition_violation.analysis: Line 264 calculates `received = _underlyingBalance() - balanceBefore`. Line 266 checks `if (received == 0) revert UnderlyingPullFailed()`. Actual received amount is used, not requested amount.

faulty_error_handling.analysis: SafeERC20.safeTransferFrom reverts on failure. Additionally, received == 0 check catches edge cases.

counterexample.scenario: Wrap with fee-on-transfer token
preconditions: Underlying is FoT token with 1% fee
attack_steps: User gets zERC20 for actual 99 received
counterexample.expected_result: User gets zERC20 proportional to actual received
counterexample.actual_behavior: Code handles FoT tokens correctly via balance delta calculation

audit_results.rationale: FoT tokens ARE handled via balance delta calculation. Received amount is used for all subsequent calculations. Deployment policy may still prohibit FoT for other reasons.

audit_results.title: ACTION-LM-MINT-ZERC20 requires authorized minter

input_validation_bypass.attack_vector: Call mint() from unauthorized address
input_validation_bypass.analysis: mint() checks `if (msg.sender != minter()) revert OnlyMinter()` at line 186. Only configured minter (LiquidityManager) can mint. No bypass via inheritance or delegatecall.

state_transition_violation.attack_vector: Minter set to malicious address
state_transition_violation.analysis: setMinter is onlyOwner. Owner can set any minter. This is OUT OF SCOPE per trust model.

faulty_error_handling.analysis: Authorization uses revert. _mint from OZ ERC20 reverts on overflow. No silent failures.

race_conditions.attack_vector: Race between setMinter and mint call
race_conditions.analysis: If owner changes minter during pending mint, the mint reverts with OnlyMinter. Safe behavior.

counterexample.scenario: Attacker deploys malicious contract that calls mint()
counterexample.actual_behavior: Correctly reverts for non-minter callers

audit_results.rationale: CRITICAL. Minting authorization correctly enforced. Only configured minter can call mint(). Owner-controlled minter setting is out of scope.
